issues.t: Distributor failure causes stalling or no-start
issues.sym: The engine stalls at low speed or at stops, idles roughly, misfires, or cranks without starting.
issues.why: The distributor on this engine is a known weak point as it ages, and a failing unit interrupts spark.
issues.next: Have the ignition system tested before replacing parts at random; a worn distributor is a common finding on these cars.

issues.t: Pre-catalytic converter breakdown and oil consumption
issues.sym: Oil level drops between changes, blue smoke, a rattle from the exhaust manifold area, loss of power or a check engine light for the catalyst.
issues.why: The small converter built into the exhaust manifold can overheat and break apart. Pieces can be pulled back into the cylinders and score them, which leads to heavy oil burning. Early 2002 cars were also recalled for an exhaust fire risk tied to the catalyst.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and do not let it run low. Get any manifold rattle or catalyst code checked right away, and confirm the 2002 recall was done.

issues.t: Engine stalls from crankshaft or camshaft sensor fault (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning at low speed, or the car is hard to start, misfires, or runs with a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor can overheat and drop its signal for a moment, too briefly for the computer to flag it, and the engine stops. An earlier recall covered poorly welded crank and cam sensors.
issues.next: Have a Nissan dealer check your VIN for the engine computer update and sensor recalls. If the car stalls, stop driving it until it is checked.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure and misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire code, shaking at idle, bucking under acceleration and worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The coil-on-plug ignition coils on this engine wear out with age and are a frequent repair on these cars.
issues.next: Have the misfiring cylinder identified and the bad coil replaced; replace old spark plugs at the same time. A flashing check engine light means stop soon to protect the converter.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; an airbag light may be on.
issues.why: Some driver airbag modules were built with a defect that could keep them from deploying in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a Nissan dealer replace the module if it has not been done.

issues.t: CVT shudder, whine or failure
issues.sym: Shudder or slipping when pulling away, a whine or hum that rises with speed, and weak or delayed acceleration.
issues.why: The early Nissan CVT in this generation has a record of wear, with more complaints on 2007-2009 cars. Nissan's extended CVT warranty for 2003-2010 CVT models has largely run out.
issues.next: Use only the correct Nissan CVT fluid and change it on schedule. Get a diagnosis at the first shudder or whine before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Steering lock failure, car won't start
issues.sym: Push-button start does nothing, the steering wheel stays locked, and a key or steering warning shows on the dash.
issues.why: The electronic steering column lock can fail to release, and the car will not start while it reads locked. Nissan ran a service campaign on this part.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer whether the steering lock campaign applies to your VIN. The lock unit usually needs replacing and a tow may be required.

issues.t: Passenger airbag switches off with an adult seated (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light stays on even when an adult is in the seat.
issues.why: A part in the passenger seat occupant sensor was out of spec and could interrupt its signal, so the system thinks the seat is empty.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Until it is repaired, avoid putting an adult in the front passenger seat when the OFF light is on.

issues.t: Front strut mount insulator can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking or clunking from the front suspension over bumps.
issues.why: Some upper strut insulators were out of spec and can crack, letting the strut rod work loose from its mount and affecting control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the front struts inspected promptly if you hear knocking. Do not ignore a new clunk from the front end.

issues.t: Loose suspension and steering rack bolts (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps or a loose, vague feel in the steering.
issues.why: On some cars built in mid-2012, bolts holding suspension and steering parts were not tightened to spec at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the bolts inspected before driving much further if the steering feels loose.

issues.t: CVT judder, hesitation or failure
issues.sym: Judder or vibration when accelerating, hesitation, surging, whining, a transmission warning light, or in some cases loss of drive.
issues.why: The CVT in these cars has a long complaint record. Nissan issued a bulletin for judder with codes P17F0 or P17F1 on 4-cylinder cars, and class-action settlements extended CVT coverage on 2013-2018 models to 7 years or 84,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer about the judder bulletin and whether any extended coverage still applies to your VIN. Get a diagnosis at the first shudder.

issues.t: Hood can fly open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood lifts slightly after being closed, or is not held by the safety catch after the release lever is pulled.
issues.why: The secondary hood latch can corrode or bind and stay open. Several earlier recalls on 2013-2015 cars did not fully cure it, so Nissan recalled 2013-2018 cars again.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open hood latch recalls. Always confirm the hood is fully latched before driving, and do not drive if it will not stay latched.

issues.t: Rear door can open when the window is lowered (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door unlatches or pops open when its window goes down.
issues.why: The rear door latch cable could be routed wrong at the factory and pulls the latch when the window moves.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Use the child locks and keep rear windows up until the repair is done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may turn off with an adult seated (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light comes on even though an adult is sitting there.
issues.why: The occupant classification system can misread an adult as a child or an empty seat, so the airbag would not deploy.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both occupant-sensor recalls. Until fixed, avoid seating an adult in front when the OFF light is on.

issues.t: Backup camera image can disappear (recall)
issues.sym: No rear camera picture when backing up after a display setting was changed.
issues.why: Certain display settings can switch off the rear camera image and it stays off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the software updated. Look behind you directly when reversing until then.

issues.t: VC-Turbo engine bearing failure (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, loss of power, or the engine quitting while driving. In rare cases oil escapes and catches fire.
issues.why: Some engine bearings were made with defects that can lead to engine failure. A federal investigation covered 2019-2021 cars, and Nissan recalled 2019-2020 cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the engine software update done. If you hear knocking or lose power, pull over safely and have the car towed.

issues.t: Fuel line clip may not be locked (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell under the hood, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A clip connecting the low-pressure fuel line to the high-pressure pump may not have been locked at the factory, so fuel can leak.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have the car checked. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rearview camera image flickers or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture flickers, looks distorted, or is missing.
issues.why: The camera wiring harness can be damaged and lose its connection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Look behind you directly when reversing until it is repaired.

issues.t: Tie rod nut may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering, or the car pulling.
issues.why: The nut on the outer tie rod ball joint may not have been tightened properly, and the joint could separate from the steering knuckle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the steering feels loose or clunks, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Door striker may break (recall)
issues.sym: A door does not latch firmly or feels loose when closed.
issues.why: Some door strikers were poorly welded and can break, which could let a door open while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Do not drive with a door that will not latch firmly.

issues.t: Front passenger airbags may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The wrong fasteners were used to mount the passenger and knee airbags.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have a Nissan dealer make the repair as soon as possible.
